item.text: {"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"During 2023, Tshisekedi clearly exercised appointment and personnel-management authority: he reshuffled the cabinet in March, retaining the prime minister and assigning senior portfolios including defense, interior, economy, justice, finance, planning, and infrastructure (BATCH-0009-E003); issued presidential judicial ordinances that promoted, appointed, reassigned, dismissed, and retired civilian and military magistrates (BATCH-0015-E006; BATCH-0019-E005; BATCH-0019-E006); and appointed or reconfirmed managers and boards across public enterprises and regulatory bodies in July (BATCH-0008-E014). He also received a newly appointed Gécamines board and management team and their work plan, while giving management guidance (BATCH-0018-E004). These records establish control over appointments, some retention, and formal placement of personnel across key institutions, but they do not establish selection criteria, appointee capability, effective empowerment, subsequent performance, or systematic replacement in response to failure. The personnel record is therefore mixed: the government’s reported transfer of surrendered Mobondo fighters into military training without vetting, and broader support for abusive armed groups and private military personnel, raise concerns about screening and suitability, although the available evidence does not attribute every individual decision directly to Tshisekedi (BATCH-0010-E015; BATCH-0011-E002; BATCH-0028-E016). The April 2024 appointment of Judith Suminwa is outside the 2023 period and is excluded from the substantive assessment (BATCH-0005-E004; BATCH-0012-R11-E003;
